page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7nex.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this instance utilizes an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration features 2 physical cores with a dedicated CPU allocation and 1.0 thread per core. It includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but notable limitations in multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1880.59 and Geekbench single-core score of 1519.0 fall within the average range. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 27.64 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.43 GB/sec also demonstrate moderate throughput. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1931.67 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1774.0, both placing in the lower tier. Memory bandwidth is also limited, registering 14.51 GB/sec for large block reads and 13.41 GB/sec for large block writes.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.g7nex.large lies in its low multi-core scaling and weak memory subsystem performance, as evidenced by a Passmark memory score of 1629.41 and database operations score of 997.36. While the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent single-core execution without noisy-neighbor interference, the overall resource density makes it less efficient for memory-bound or highly parallelized workloads. Qualitatively, this instance represents a basic entry-level tier for dedicated compute resources, where cost efficiency is optimized for workloads that do not demand high memory throughput or parallel processing. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, and low-concurrency development environments.
